speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. When did you deliver, and on which day did the fever and abdominal tenderness begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge, and have you developed any chills or nausea? I need to assess for signs of endometritis or other postpartum infections.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning when you urinate, or any flank pain that might suggest a kidney infection? I also need to know if your vaginal discharge has any foul odor, which would point toward endometritis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have dysuria or flank pain, and is there any foul-smelling lochia? I need to differentiate between endometritis and a urinary tract infection. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: I see the CBC is pending. Have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and are you experiencing pain or burning when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The new symptom of breathing difficulty is concerning for a pulmonary embolism, especially given the recent delivery and large infant size. I will request a D-dimer test and a CT pulmonary angiogram to rule out this life-threatening condition. REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer, REQUEST TEST: CT_Pulmonary_Angiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal pulmonary workup, I suspect the breathing difficulty is secondary to pain from severe uterine tenderness and decreased bowel sounds, likely due to endometritis. I will request a pelvic ultrasound to assess for retained products of conception or abscess. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the imaging is normal, I need to confirm if your lochia has a foul odor, as this is the hallmark sign of endometritis. Please also clarify if you have had a fever over 38°C since delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the imaging is normal and urinary symptoms are denied, the combination of fever, uterine tenderness, and prolonged labor strongly points to endometritis. I will proceed with a presumptive diagnosis and initiate treatment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometritis
